title: Agentic AI for plant operations: From dashboards to decisions
summary: Microsoft explores how AI assistants can connect engineering documents, maintenance history, and operating data. A Yara example illustrates the role of an operational digital twin in making plant knowledge easier to use.
takeaway: Before choosing an agent, map the information an operator needs to resolve one recurring problem and define who approves its recommendations.
context: Vendor perspective with customer-reported outcomes; results are specific to the implementations described.

title: 2026 State of Smart Manufacturing Report
summary: Rockwell's eleventh annual study examines manufacturers' adoption of digital technologies, AI, and cybersecurity. Its publisher summary describes a survey of 1,560 respondents across 17 countries, conducted with Sapio Research.
takeaway: Use the findings to frame a discussion about your plant's data utilization, integration gaps, and readiness to scale a successful pilot.
context: Vendor-sponsored survey. This brief draws on the public report highlights and release announcement; respondent expectations are not guaranteed outcomes.

title: 4 ways AI is enabling the future of industrial work
summary: This collection looks at how industrial companies apply AI to demanding workflows. Its ARUM example describes converting machining expertise into software that helps translate CAD designs into machine instructions.
takeaway: Look for specialist knowledge that repeatedly delays a workflow, then ask how experienced staff could help document and validate it.
context: Customer stories published by the technology supplier, useful for ideas rather than independent performance comparisons.

title: Dassault Systèmes and NVIDIA Partner to Build Industrial AI Platform Powering Virtual Twins
summary: NVIDIA and Dassault Systèmes outline a partnership combining virtual twins, accelerated computing, and AI. Their proposed architecture spans engineering simulation, production systems, and assistants grounded in industrial knowledge.
takeaway: When evaluating a digital twin, identify the physical behavior it must model and how your team would validate its predictions.
context: A partnership announcement describing intended capabilities, not an independent benchmark or proof of deployment at your plant.

title: Global Lighthouse Network: Rewiring Operations for Resilience and Impact at Scale
summary: The Forum's 2026 white paper brings together lessons from its manufacturing Lighthouse community. It focuses on operational resilience, the adoption of AI across connected operations, and the transition from local pilots to enterprise capabilities.
takeaway: Read this when a pilot works on one line but stalls across sites: the useful questions concern ownership, people, and repeatable deployment.
context: Examples from selected leading sites, rather than a representative sample of every manufacturer. Summary based on the publisher's overview.
relatedLabel: Turn the reading into a roadmap

title: Siemens' AI powered Nanjing facility named World Economic Forum Global Lighthouse Factory
summary: Siemens describes its Nanjing plant's response to changing orders and shorter delivery windows. The site combined digital twins, modular automation, manufacturing operations management, and AI applications in a broader transformation program.
takeaway: Treat this as a systems example: connect production planning, execution, and feedback before attributing improvements to any single AI application.
context: A factory case study in a Siemens press release. Reported improvements belong to the combined transformation program.
